facts.statement: The genus Candidodon was described by Carvalho and Campos in 1988.
Fossils of Candidodon date to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
Candidodon lived between 119.57 and 93.9 million years ago, spanning the Aptian to Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Cenomanian (119.57 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Candidodon is classified as a reptile.
Fossils of Candidodon have been found in the Early Cretaceous Itapecuru and Alcântara Formations in Brazil.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Early Cretaceous Itapecuru Formation and Alcântara Formation in Brazil.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Mariliasuchus belongs to the family Comahuesuchidae; if so, Candidodon would be the sole member of the family Candidodontidae.
facts.quote: a recent phylogenetic analysis has shown that Mariliasuchus may instead be closer in relation to Comahuesuchus than to Candidodon and thus a member of the family Comahuesuchidae. If this is true, Candidodon would be the only member of the family Candidodontidae.
